title: CyberLawAssist: System Overview, Plan Comparison, and ISO/IEC 25010:2011 Readiness Assessment

blocks.text: 1. Executive summary

CyberLawAssist is a local web-based legal information and office-support system for the Muntinlupa City District Office - Public Attorney's Office. It combines a public introduction, role-specific workspaces, an offline retrieval chatbot, legal information, personal preparation tools, and staff-managed support and intake records.

The current implementation goes beyond the earliest browser-only analyzer concept. Later owner instructions introduced server-backed User/Admin accounts, Live support, physical intake, database reports, formatted Word exports, and supporting interface utilities. Guest history remains browser-local; signed-in activity is associated with the authenticated database account.

Assessment conclusion: the source shows substantial implementation relevant to ISO/IEC 25010:2011, particularly the intended workflows, role/ownership controls, and user error protection. Overall measured quality has not been established. A numerical ISO score, a blanket pass, or a certification claim would not be supported by the available evidence.

Confirmed feedback: the project owner reports that Live support works and previously accepted the frontend design. The owner also assigns chatbot accuracy and legal-content review to the group and considers those activities complete. This report does not repeat that review or invent numerical results for it.
2. Review basis and evidence labels

Snapshot: 18 October 2026. This report uses the current project source, local planning documents, implementation notes, and the owner's statements in the project conversation. It is an implementation overview and a source-based readiness assessment, not an independent penetration test, usability study, performance benchmark, or formal ISO evaluation.

blocks.text: The 2011 standard is used because that is the version requested and referenced in the planning materials. Its product model has eight quality areas; quality in use is considered separately. ISO currently marks this edition withdrawn and lists newer related editions. This report does not substitute the 2023 model for the requested 2011 assessment. [ISO-1, ISO-2]
3. Purpose, users, and boundaries

The system helps people describe cyber-related concerns in ordinary language, browse information under RA 10175, organize preparation steps, and contact office staff. It supports public information and office coordination; it does not decide guilt, legal liability, eligibility for representation, or a case outcome.

A chatbot reply, a decision-guide result, a saved checklist, or a Word export does not itself file a complaint, schedule an appointment, or establish an attorney-client relationship. The office must confirm official actions and assistance.

rows: Office

Muntinlupa City District Office - Public Attorney's Office. Ground Floor, Municipal City Hall of Justice Building, Right Wing, National Road, Tunasan, Muntinlupa, 1773 Metro Manila. Phone: (02) 8862 2525.
Interface languages
English and Tagalog are supported by the workspace translation layer. Public legal-policy and error-page copy is currently English; a complete multilingual coverage assessment was not performed.
Chatbot languages
English, Tagalog, and Taglish; explicit selection and heuristic automatic detection.
Device scope
Responsive desktop/sidebar and mobile/bottom-navigation layouts. CSS implementation does not establish usability or compatibility on every actual device.
Operating context
XAMPP Apache/PHP and MariaDB on the host computer, plus the local Python service. Phones on the same network access the web host; they do not need direct access to the Python port.

blocks.text: 4. Features by role

rows: Guest
Chatbot, suggested prompts, conversation rename/pin/delete, decision guide, RA 10175 guide, public notifications, and office information.
No account required. Conversation history and Guest read/preferences data use the current browser profile. No Live support, signed-in checklist, or administrator tools.
User

Guest information features plus personal SQL-backed chat history, saved checklist, checklist-only printing, Word checklist export, alerts, notifications/read markers, personal profile/settings/language, password change, and Live support.
Public signup creates Users only. Private account data is requested under the authenticated user ID and is not shared with other Users.
Admin

Dashboard, physical intake, searchable/paginated case records, record details/editing/status, User directory and account management, admin creation, Live support inbox/replies, and weekly/monthly/yearly reports with Word export. Admin also has an own-account chatbot/checklist/history.

Admin accounts are created by signed-in administrators and have unique admin numbers. Office records and support conversations are available to staff; the application does not provide a screen for browsing another account's private AI history.

blocks.text: 5. Main workflows

Public entry: Home introduces the office, explains how the system helps, links the law guide without forcing login, and offers Guest access or registration/login. Office information is presented before account workflows.

Chatbot: the user enters a message or chooses a suggested topic, selects a reply language, and receives a locally retrieved answer, sources, suggestions, or a clarification/error state. History supports rename, pin, and confirmed deletion. Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a new line. The current keyboard handler also avoids submitting while text composition is active or a send is already busy/disabled.
Decision guide: a separate guided flow gathers selections and organizes next steps. It is distinct from the chatbot and is not a formal legal decision engine.

Live support: a signed-in User sends an office message. An Admin selects that User conversation from the inbox and replies. Guests do not appear in the inbox. Messages and related notifications are stored in SQL. Visible support pages poll approximately every five seconds; actual end-to-end latency also depends on the server and connection.

Checklist: items and completion states are saved to the signed-in account. Word export includes office identification, generation date, progress totals, and an item/status table. Printing targets the checklist rather than the whole portal.

Office intake: staff record a walk-in visit, concern category, date, contact details when supplied, assigned staff, status, and brief factual notes. Records are saved in case_records and viewed through Case records. A walk-in does not need a User account. The creator reference identifies the staff account, not an automatic link to an online User.

Reports: weekly output covers Monday to Sunday; monthly output follows the actual calendar month, including leap-year February; annual output has twelve monthly buckets. Figures use saved visit dates and exclude records without a visit date. Weekly/monthly/yearly Word exports use the selected report period and the same summary/bucket calculation as the screen.

Account administration: Manage account supports User status changes and password changes. Permanent User deletion requires the administrator password and the literal DELETE confirmation, removes linked personal activity in a transaction, and is blocked for an account retained as an office record creator. New Admin creation keeps the creating administrator signed in. Admin numbers are identifiers, not an additional authentication factor.
6. Architecture and persistence

rows: pages/ and index.html
Public HTML and thin role/tab wrappers. PHP checks protected page access before serving their HTML.
assets/js/portal.js
Shared role navigation, rendering, form handling, state coordination, polling, and calls to the same-origin API. Navigation changes tabs without reloading the entire shell.
assets/php/auth.php and bootstrap.php
Sessions, login/admin-number login, public User registration, password hashing, CSRF, input validation, current-user/role checks, and shared account creation.
assets/php/api.php and data.php
Authenticated feature actions, ownership checks, SQL-backed data, support inbox, account administration, intake, and report queries.
assets/php/docx.php
Locally generated OOXML Word packages, letterhead, tables, document metadata, and page footer. Temporary package files are outside the web root and removed after generation.
phyton ai/
Local retrieval engine and English/Tagalog/Taglish datasets. A FastAPI adapter exists; the launcher uses the built-in HTTP server when FastAPI/Uvicorn are unavailable.
database/
Installation schema, additive migrations, seed content, and the database plan. Installation and migration scripts are CLI-only.
extra/ and root sw.js
Skeleton loaders, public-file browser caching, offline notice, policy/error presentation, and supporting documentation. Root .htaccess holds permanent aliases and the 404 handler.

blocks.text: Request flow: Browser -> Apache/PHP -> MariaDB for account and office records. Chatbot flow: Browser -> PHP -> local Python retrieval service -> PHP -> Browser. Guest history is saved in browser storage after the response; signed-in history is saved under the actual account ID in SQL.

The schema has twelve application tables: users; chat_conversations; chat_messages; support_threads; support_messages; checklist_items; case_records; notifications; notification_reads; law_topics; law_translations; office_contacts. There are not separate duplicated Guest/User/Admin copies of every table.

The local corpus contains 1,023 Q&A records per language, 3,069 total. Its construction is 50 scenarios by 20 facets plus 23 FAQs per language. It uses normalized text, TF-IDF-style indexed word/bigram retrieval, character matching, and limited follow-up context. It is retrieval software, not a generative LLM. Dataset quantity and similarity scores do not establish legal correctness or measured classification accuracy.
7. What changed from the earlier plans

The original System Plan, the UI/UX plan, the TXT note, and the later UI Design System represent different planning stages. The UI/UX plan itself has conflicting assumptions: it lists Guest/User/Admin in one place but also specifies no login and excludes accounts later; it mentions three languages while listing Tagalog/Taglish input out of scope. Current behavior follows the owner's later explicit implementation requests rather than silently treating every draft statement as simultaneously binding.

8. Later additions now present

Account improvements include User-only public registration, a dedicated Admin login, unique admin numbers, admin-managed Admin creation, role-locked pages, profile/settings/language menus, and logout. User management includes password changes, disabling/enabling, and confirmed deletion.

Interaction improvements include persisted history, rename/pin/delete controls, in-app delete confirmation, suggestions inside the chatbot, a separate decision guide, keyboard send/newline behavior, responsive bottom navigation, and a selectable Admin support inbox. Live support has been reported working by the owner.

Office/data improvements include MariaDB persistence, intake references, case editing/revision checks, searching and pagination, calendar-based reports, Word formatting, and checklist-only printing. Security-related additions include CSRF checks, session regeneration, login throttling, ownership checks, session invalidation, and account identity binding in API calls.

Supporting additions include workspace/report skeleton loaders, a public-file cache with a cache-clear control, an offline notice, revised Terms/Privacy pages, server-validated registration acknowledgement with version/time, a custom graphic 404, and permanent redirects for obsolete public URL names. Private API responses and protected workspace HTML are excluded from the service-worker cache.
9. ISO/IEC 25010:2011 product-quality assessment

The following are desk-review judgments about the present implementation. They are not measured pass/fail results. ISO provides the evaluation model; the project must define its own relevant targets, collect evidence, and document the evaluation context. [ISO-1, ISO-2]

rows: Functional suitability

Substantial role workflows exist: legal information, chatbot, guide, history, checklist, support, intake, account controls and reports. Owner confirms Live support. Some original workflows were adapted; content/notice authoring is not complete.
Map the final accepted scope to demonstrated scenarios. Attach the group's existing NLP/content results. Record expected/actual results for current account, export, case, and report actions.
Performance efficiency

Retrieval indexes are prepared in memory; cases are paginated; public assets can be reused. Support polling has a five-second interval. These design choices do not prove response-time or resource targets.
Measure median and high-percentile latency, CPU, RAM, and behavior at an agreed concurrent-user count. Long histories, full support payloads, and the User directory need capacity checks.
Compatibility
Browser-to-PHP-to-SQL/Python interfaces and Word output are implemented. Owner reports a working User/Admin support exchange.
Record browser/OS/device coverage and open Word exports in the intended office software. Document the active Python server adapter and integration versions.
Usability
Owner has accepted the design. Role navigation, plain-language labels, mobile layout, keyboard sending, confirmation dialogs, skeletons, and reduced-motion options are present.
Observe actual target users completing tasks. Measure task success/time and navigation errors. Review keyboard focus, screen-reader use, contrast, tap sizes, and the coverage of translations.
Reliability
Transactions, request keys, duplicate-prevention logic, retry states, revision checks, and local backups support recovery. No high-availability service or demonstrated restore result is established.
Record server/AI outage handling, interrupted saves, duplicate retries, concurrent edits, and restoration from an isolated backup. Define recovery-time/data-loss expectations before measuring.
Security

Password hashes, session cookies, CSRF, prepared queries, role/ownership checks, login limits and administrator reauthentication for sensitive User actions are visible in source. Public cache excludes private endpoints.

Perform role/ownership and session abuse checks. Verify deployment transport and host/database access. A tamper-evident action audit, cryptographic signatures, and measured resistance to attack are not established; admin number alone is not MFA.
Maintainability

PHP auth/data/document helpers, Python engine/corpus modules, and schema/migrations are separated. Documentation exists. portal.js concentrates many workflows, and older regression assertions still mention CSV.

Bring tests/documentation into line with Word exports and current API contracts. Establish a repeatable regression procedure and change traceability. Profile/refactor only where measurements or change risk justify it.
Portability
The app has local startup/setup instructions and a Python fallback adapter. Standard browser, PHP, SQL and Word interfaces support deployment options.

Demonstrate a clean installation on another host. Document first-admin provisioning and dependency versions. Renaming the project requires changes to RewriteBase/ErrorDocument and absolute 404/offline paths; LAN HTTP does not activate the service worker.

blocks.text: Direct answer: the implementation shows good alignment in several quality areas, but it cannot honestly be rated as an overall ISO/IEC 25010:2011 pass from source inspection and one confirmed workflow. Performance, reliability, security assurance, accessibility, compatibility, and quality-in-use claims require recorded evaluation results.
10. Quality in use: separate outcome assessment

The 2011 quality-in-use model considers effectiveness, efficiency, satisfaction, freedom from risk, and context coverage. These concern outcomes for real users in a stated environment, so a source-code checklist alone is insufficient. [ISO-2]

rows: Effectiveness
The owner reports successful Live support. Other workflow completion rates are not recorded here.
Task completion, correct output, and error counts for representative users and agreed scenarios.
Efficiency
No measured task duration or effort comparison is attached.
Time and number of actions needed to find a law, prepare a checklist, contact staff, and complete intake.
Satisfaction
Design acceptance and positive Live support feedback are qualitative evidence, not a population satisfaction score.
Approved user questionnaire, respondent context, and documented comments without invented scores.
Freedom from risk
Informational disclaimers, limited sharing, account controls, confirmation, and support escalation can reduce some risks. Actual harm reduction is not measured.
Review misleading guidance, accidental deletion/disclosure, shared-device use, and interpretation of exports with office stakeholders.
Context coverage
Desktop/mobile CSS and localhost/LAN operation are intended contexts. Offline AI still needs the reachable local host; LAN HTTP lacks service-worker caching.
Observe the agreed device, network, role, language, and accessibility contexts and record unsupported conditions.

blocks.text: 11. Evaluation and acceptance evidence to collect

This is a proposed evidence plan, not a claim that these checks were executed. Thresholds and scoring weights should come from the approved project instrument or be agreed with stakeholders; the numerical targets below are intentionally not invented as ISO requirements.

rows: Functional acceptance

For each final requirement: scenario ID, role, preconditions, expected output, observed output, date/device, and result. Include signup consent, admin number uniqueness, role URL protection, history controls, checklist print/export, intake revisions, report periods, and account management.
Existing group work
Attach the group's approved content/NLP review and any existing language-specific accuracy results. Do not equate 3,069 records or a retrieval similarity score with correctness.
Live support

Keep the owner's confirmation and add a reproducible normal-window User / private-window Admin conversation record, including inbox selection and reply. Do not assume two normal tabs represent different accounts.
Performance/capacity
Record the host specification, active Python adapter, dataset size, browser count, workload, measured response times, CPU/RAM, and failures. Compare results to project-approved targets.
Recovery

Restore a backup into an isolated database and record the result; do not overwrite the working project to demonstrate recovery. Record service-outage, interrupted-send, retry, and concurrent-edit behavior.
Security/access

Record negative role/ownership cases with separate accounts, invalid CSRF, stale sessions, and account disable/delete behavior. Confirm HTTPS and network access choices for any deployment beyond localhost.
User evaluation

Use the capstone-approved instrument with IT evaluators and representative users. Keep the sample/context and analysis method explicit. A small informal usability walkthrough is not automatically a statistically representative ISO score.
Document/browser behavior
Open actual checklist/report Word downloads in the intended office Word processor. Inspect mobile overflow, keyboard sending, 404 recovery and actual HTTP statuses for missing/redirected URLs.
Policy adoption

Confirm the new Terms/Privacy wording, retention/backup rules, office branding/contact authority, and record handling before public adoption. This is separate from repeating the group's already-owned NLP/content review.

blocks.text: 12. Known limits and exclusions

The chatbot does not generate unrestricted answers, update laws automatically, decide cases, file complaints, or learn itself from conversations. Automatic language selection is heuristic. No external cloud AI, email/SMS delivery integration, or emergency-response guarantee is configured.

The admin area currently displays seeded legal/office content and notices; it does not provide the complete proposed Knowledge Base and general notification publishing editor. Physical intake is a saved-record workflow, not a fully demonstrated real-time queue system with the earlier Waiting/In service statuses.

There is no automatic record-retention schedule in the current implementation. Account deletion does not remove prior backups or downloaded/printed documents. A full staff action audit and formal security validation are not provided by the current evidence.

Responsive code, a public cache, and a launcher do not prove cross-device portability, uptime, restore success, accessibility compliance, or an office production deployment. This report contains no fabricated Alpha/Beta results, numeric ISO rating, participant count, or test pass rate.
13. Practical handover and operation

Start the local project through start-project.bat. Keep Apache, MariaDB, and the Python service running for their corresponding features. Use the dedicated Admin login with an assigned admin number; public signup is User-only. Existing administrator numbers are visible in Profile and the Administrators list.

For same-computer Live support, use a normal browser User session and an incognito/different-browser Admin session on the same localhost project. For a phone on the same network, use the host computer's LAN address. Do not expose the Python or database port solely to make the web UI work; PHP forwards local requests.

Keep the private configuration and backups outside htdocs. Back up before schema migrations. Store downloaded case-related documents securely. On a fresh installation, establish or restore an authorized initial Admin account before using admin-managed account creation.

When editing policies, update the document dates, signup policy_version field, and CLA_POLICY_VERSION together. When the project URL changes, update the documented redirect/error paths. Asset cache versions are project-specific; cache contents do not substitute for server/database backups.
